text.p: Fibreboard Corp., the building products manufacturer, said Monday it reached a final agreement with its insurance companies on claims of more than $3 billion in asbestos lawsuits.

The company said that under agreement with its insurers -- CNA Financial Corp.'s Continental Casualty Co. and Chubb Corp.'s Pacific Indemnity Co. all asbestos-related injury liabilities of Fibreboard will be paid through insurance funds and existing corporate reserves.
The U.S. Fifth Circuit Court approved the agreement in July, which requires its insurance firms to pay all settlements reached prior to Aug. 27, 1993.

The settlement "is a major milestone in resolving our asbestos litigation and continuing Fibreboard's turn-around strategy," said Fibreboard Chief Executive John D. Roach. "We now know for the first time that we are assured at a minimum of receiving the enormous benefits provided by the insurance settlement agreement."
Fibreboard's stock was up 37.5 cents at $33.25 on the American Stock Exchange.
